report.summary: Chunk 3 of 9: defines helper functions for inventory, including digest check, area, dotted name, method suffix, pyproject scanning, disk packages, and orphan bytecode detection.
risks: _pyproject_packages | medium | Line scanner for TOML may miss complex configurations (e.g., inline tables) or produce incorrect results for nested tables; the comment acknowledges this but it's a potential source of bugs. | Review whether the line scanner handles all valid TOML package specifications used in the project; consider adding a fallback to a real TOML parser if available.

handoff.purpose: Define helper functions for inventory analysis: digest validation, area derivation, dotted name conversion, method suffix lookup, pyproject.toml package scanning, on-disk package discovery, and orphan bytecode detection.

symbols.name: _area_of
symbols.note: Returns the parent directory of a relative path, or '(repo root)' if no slash.

symbols.name: _dotted
symbols.note: Converts a relative file path (possibly ending in .py or __init__) to a dotted module name.

symbols.name: _method_of
symbols.note: Returns the method name corresponding to a function name suffix using _METHOD_BY_SUFFIX.

symbols.name: _pyproject_packages
symbols.note: Scans pyproject.toml for a [tool.setuptools] packages array using a line scanner; returns sorted unique package names or empty list on error.

symbols.name: _packages_on_disk
symbols.note: Walks directories under distribution roots to find packages (directories with __init__.py) that exist on disk.

symbols.name: _orphan_bytecode
symbols.note: Finds __pycache__ directories whose parent has no .py files, indicating orphaned bytecode.

claims.why: The function returns a list of strings from that TOML array, or an empty list on error.

claims.text: A line scanner rather than a TOML parser: this module is stdlib-only across 3.10 (no ``tomllib``), and the shape being read is one array under one known table.
claims.why: The code uses line-by-line matching with regexes, not a TOML parser, and the module only imports stdlib.

claims.text: An unreadable or absent pyproject yields an empty list, which both detectors below read as "no promise was made" -- never as a finding.
claims.why: The function returns [] on OSError, and the doc says it's never taken as a finding.

claims.text: Dotted packages that exist under the distribution roots the metadata already names.
claims.why: The function takes listed names, extracts distribution roots, and walks them to find packages.

claims.text: Scoped to those roots on purpose: every directory in the repo with an ``__init__.py`` is not a candidate for the wheel, and treating a fixture or a runs/ directory as one would manufacture findings.
claims.why: The function only walks directories derived from listed roots, not the entire repo.

claims.text: ``__pycache__`` directories holding bytecode whose sources are gone.
claims.why: The function returns tuples of (path, count) for __pycache__ dirs whose parent has no .py files.

claims.text: The exact shape of the ``daedalus/hermes`` remnant the hand-written inventory recorded: the package was deleted, the ``.pyc`` files stayed, and an import of the dotted name could still resolve.
claims.why: The code does not reference daedalus/hermes; this is an example, not a checkable claim.

claims.text: A cache beside live sources is not a finding -- only one with NO sibling ``.py`` at all.
claims.why: The function skips __pycache__ if the parent has any .py files (siblings list non-empty).

observations.what: Function _pyproject_packages uses a line scanner to parse TOML, which may fail on complex TOML structures (e.g., inline tables) or produce incorrect results for non-standard formatting.
Function _dotted handles .py and __init__ but not other extensions (e.g., .pyi) explicitly; if .pyi files appear, they will be treated as .py.
Function _method_of depends on _METHOD_BY_SUFFIX which is not defined in this chunk; its behavior is uncheckable.
Function _orphan_bytecode only checks for .py files in the parent directory, not .pyw or other source files; might miss orphan bytecode if only .pyw sources existed.
